parts.text: Which claim correctly states how he should report the length more accurately?

options.text: Report $5\,\mathrm{cm}$, because the tip has not reached $6\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Split the $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ gap into equal smaller parts and count how many the tip passes.
Treat the printed $5$ on the bookmark as the measured length.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Lalit measures a bookmark on a ruler marked only in centimetres. The tip sits between the $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ marks.

part_answers.answer: The tip falls between whole-centimetre marks, so the $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ unit interval must be split into equal smaller parts and those parts counted.

teacher.key_rationale: Between whole marks, equal smaller parts of the same centimetre interval are needed for a more accurate length.
